spec.question: What broad hostile control can most efficiently detect fixture assistance, semantic leakage, or old-owner misattribution across the frontier campaign?
spec.incumbent: Frontier effects survive opaque relabeling and removal of oracle/caller assistance because they are grounded in operational relations and existing lawful owners.
spec.rival: One or more apparent advances depend on human-readable labels, supplied candidate/sequence structure, evaluator leakage, or an older owner already sufficient for the behavior.
spec.manipulation: Apply a common hostile wrapper to each embodied arm: independently randomize all non-causal names/IDs/orderings, remove oracle candidate/sequence hints, and run an existing-owner-only baseline under identical budgets before the proposed arm mechanism/spec.
controls: evaluation code blind to semantic labels
spec.incumbent_prediction: Valid frontier effects preserve outcome modulo opaque permutation and exceed the existing-owner-only baseline only where a genuinely new distinction is required.
spec.rival_prediction: Effects collapse under relabeling/oracle removal or are reproduced by existing owners, demoting the claimed frontier advance.
spec.measurement: Effect size across permutations, oracle dependence, existing-owner baseline parity, assistance ledger, authority trace.
spec.minimal_embodiment: Reusable test harness/wrapper applied to research fixtures only; owns no Microseed architecture.
spec.falsifier: Any claimed advance is fully reproduced by older owners or disappears when non-causal assistance is removed.
spec.loop_plus: Use failures to route back to the affected arm; K never proposes replacement architecture.
